topic.focus: momentum crash risk management and drawdown protection
topic.angle: bear-market filters, VIX gating, short-term reversal overlay

papers.title: Momentum Crashes and the 52-Week High
papers.hypothesis: Construct crash-neutral momentum by making the cross-sectional ranking orthogonal to each stock's price-to-52-week-high ratio (PTH), removing the speculative rebound component that drives momentum crashes.
papers.rationale: Published in FAJ 2023, Byun & Jeon show that stocks far from their 52-week highs disproportionately drive momentum crashes during market rebounds. Constructing residual momentum (regress 12-1mo returns on PTH, rank on residuals) achieves higher Sharpe and lower crash frequency in US and international markets. This is a signal-construction change, not a macro gate, so it is compatible with the existing walk-forward framework and costs no additional lookback data beyond what is already available.

papers.title: Short-term momentum and reversals, turnover, and a stock's price-to-52-week-high ratio
papers.hypothesis: Condition the standard skip-last-month rule on each stock's PTH and turnover: suppress the skip for high-PTH, high-turnover stocks (where short-term momentum dominates), and apply a stronger skip for low-PTH, low-turnover stocks (where reversal dominates).
papers.rationale: Chen, Stivers & Sun (2024, JEF) demonstrate that the well-known 1-month reversal switches to continuation for stocks with simultaneously high price-to-52-week-high and high share turnover. This means the blanket skip-21-day rule throws away real signal for a subset of winners. Segmenting the universe on these two dimensions before applying the skip can recover alpha and reduce crash exposure by avoiding the most reversal-prone names during rebounds.

papers.title: Avoid Equity Bear Markets with a Market Timing Strategy
papers.source: https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=4397638 | SSRN Working Paper, Ďurian & Vojtko, March 2023
papers.hypothesis: Apply a 200-day SMA bear-market gate on the broad index (SPY/IWB): when index price is below its 200-day SMA, scale down or fully flatten the long side of the momentum portfolio rather than holding through the drawdown.
papers.rationale: Ďurian & Vojtko (SSRN 2023) test a composite bear-market timing model whose core signal is a 200-day SMA on the broad equity index; applied from 1927-2023, it more than doubles the market Sharpe ratio and cuts maximum drawdown by two-thirds. As an overlay on a cross-sectional strategy, this gate is easy to implement as a binary or proportional position scalar applied daily to the long leg, adding minimal complexity and no additional signal contamination of the OOS period.

papers.title: Smoothing Out Momentum and Reversal
papers.source: https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=4955388 | Swiss Finance Institute Research Paper No. 24-47, Chitsiripanich, Paolella, Polak & Walker, 2024
papers.hypothesis: Introduce a path-dependent hold constraint that prevents rebalancing a position unless the new signal rank changes by more than a threshold delta, reducing turnover by ~95% and capping maximum drawdown to 22-49% versus 76-99% for unconstrained momentum.
papers.rationale: Chitsiripanich et al. (SFI 2024) show that a sequential portfolio optimizer with path-dependent constraints that classify assets by signal strength versus rebalancing cost reduces portfolio turnover by 95-99% relative to daily rebalancing, while improving net Sharpe by 38-149% under realistic costs. For a walk-forward strategy already incurring $20/trade commissions, a persistence constraint that holds positions through small rank fluctuations directly reduces the cost drag that penalizes high-frequency rebalancing.

papers.title: Momentum, Market Volatility, and Reversal
papers.source: https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=4342008 | SSRN Working Paper, Butt, Kolari & Sadaqat, 2023
papers.hypothesis: Scale cross-sectional momentum exposure inversely with realized market volatility (e.g., 21-day rolling SPX volatility), reducing position size when vol is elevated and increasing it when vol is suppressed.
papers.rationale: Butt et al. (SSRN 2023) find that while time-series vol scaling improves time-series momentum, its benefit for cross-sectional momentum is mixed and regime-dependent — high-volatility periods that trigger scale-down often precede the strongest subsequent cross-sectional momentum, not reversals, so the gate fires at precisely the wrong time. This aligns with prior failed vol-targeting experiments in this research codebase (Session 9), confirming the result is likely negative for cross-sectional settings and suggesting volatility conditioning should be approached as a secondary signal layer rather than a direct position scalar.
